summary: Rosemary Radford Ruether was a religious studies scholar who studied at Claremont School of Theology (~1960–1965). She held a post at Howard University from circa 1965 to 1975.

Rosina Pastore is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She pursued her PhD at the University of Lausanne under the supervision of Maya Burger and Stefania Cavaliere, and has served there as an assistant and PhD candidate.

Ross Bolleter, active in Buddhist and religious studies, earned a bachelor's degree at the University of Western Australia (~1964–1967) and studied under David Tunley, John Tarrant, and Robert Baker Aitken. He served as a Zen Buddhist teacher at the Zen Group of Western Australia (~1991–2023).

Roy Rappaport was a scholar of religious studies and anthropology who completed his doctorate at Columbia University (~1959–1966). He served as Chair of Anthropology at the University of Michigan (~1965–1997) and was past president of the American Anthropological Association (~1987–1989).

Roy Tzohar works in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tel Aviv University (~1998–2005) and earned his PhD at Columbia University (~2005–2011) under Gary A. Tubb, later holding a post at Tel Aviv University (~2011).

Royall Tyler is a Japanologist who studied at Harvard University and Columbia University under Donald Keene. He held teaching posts at Ohio State, Wisconsin-Madison, and Oslo, served as head of the Japan Centre at the Australian National University (1990–2000), and was a visiting professor at Harvard.
Royce Wiles is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the Australian National University by 2000 and subsequently held a post there.

Ruben L. F. Habito is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who earned degrees from Ateneo de Manila, the University of Tokyo, and Sophia University. He held posts at Sophia University, Ryukoku University, and Southern Methodist University (1989).
Rudolf Geiger studied at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (~1913–1917). He later held an academic post at the University of Munich (~1948–1958).

Rudolf Haym worked in philosophy and history. He studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg and Frederick William University Berlin (~1839–1843), later holding a post at Halle-Wittenberg in 1868.

Rudolf Kaschewsky specialized in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies, earning degrees at the University of Bonn. He taught Tibetan at Goethe University Frankfurt and held posts at the University of Bonn from circa 1969 to 2004.
Rudolf Lange was a scholar of Japanology and linguistics. Over his career, he held academic posts at the University of Tokyo (~1874–1881) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1887–1923).
Rudolf Much was a scholar of linguistics and history who studied at the University of Vienna (~1883–1887). He spent his career on the faculty at the University of Vienna from circa 1892 to 1934.

Rudolf Otto was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology who studied at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg and under Richard von Garbe. He held posts at the University of Breslau (~1914–1917) and the University of Marburg (~1917–1929).
Rudolf Seydel worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leipzig University (~1852–1856) and subsequently held a post there from circa 1860 to 1892.

Rudolf Thurneysen was a linguist who studied at Leipzig University and under Heinrich Zimmer. He held academic posts at the University of Jena (~1882–1887), University of Freiburg (~1887–1913), and University of Bonn (~1913–1923).

Rudolf von Roth was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübinger Stift under Heinrich Ewald and in Paris under Eugène Burnouf. He held a lifelong academic career at the University of Tübingen from 1845 until 1895.

Rudrapatna Shamasastry was an Indologist educated at Sri Chamarajendra Sanskrit College, University of Madras, Oriental University, and University of Calcutta. He served as Principal of Sri Chamarajendra Sanskrit College (1912–1918) and Curator and Director at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore (1895–1929).

Ruixuan Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Supervised by Jens-Uwe Hartmann for the MA and Paul Harrison for the PhD at Leiden University (attested 2018), Chen holds a post at Heidelberg University.

Rulon Wells was a scholar of linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Utah (~1935–1939) and Harvard University (~1939–1942), and held a faculty post at Yale University from circa 1945 to 1989.
